names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 14 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Νικήτας εκ Κιέβου», with the rank word and the city left off.

death.note: saint.gr: «κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το έτος 1109 μ.Χ.», and its head line reads «Οσιος Νικητας Εκ Κιεβου (; - 1109)»; the same page dates his election to Novgorod to 1096.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 14ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Νικήτας εκ Κιέβου»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 14 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **The display name takes the see and not the calendar line's city**: saint.gr lists him as «εκ Κιέβου», out of Kyiv, where he was a monk, and its own body says he was elected bishop of Novgorod in 1096 and is buried there, so the see is what distinguishes him. **He is none of the corpus's fifteen Nicetases**, which the namesweep flagged and which were read, and he is not this run's `nicetas-the-sinaite` or `nicephorus-13-may`. **His brother is named and has no folder**: the venerable Nikon, abbot of the Lavra of Kyiv, «τιμάται 23 Μαρτίου», whom the corpus does not keep — its `nikon-` folders are other men — so he is named in the life without a link. **The page's footer links a separate commemoration of the finding of his relics**, «Ανακομιδή Ιερών λειψάνων του Αγίου Νικήτα Αρχιεπισκόπου Νόβγκοροντ», which was not read and is not recorded as a feast here; that footer also calls him archbishop, while the body says bishop, and the body is followed. **No `locations` object.** No hymn is printed.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
